title: MA2H Message (v0.6)
description: Agent->Hub message envelope. Discriminated on `type`; cross-type fields are forbidden per branch. `id` is Hub-assigned and is NOT an input. v0.5 adds the optional `to` (inter-agent addressing, spec §4/S2 grammar: first `#` terminates the agent-id segment; the session segment matches `^sess_`) and `agent.session` (spec §4.1, §16).

to.description: Optional destination (v0.5, spec §4): `agent:<id>` (principal-addressed) or `agent:<id>#<session>` (session-addressed). Absent = the human inbox, unchanged. `to: human:...` is invalid in 0.5. A `#`-bearing agent id is inexpressible here (its first `#` parses as the separator and the remainder must match `^sess_`). The Hub validates the destination at accept time (422 unknown_destination / 410 destination_gone, spec §8.1/§8.5).

body.description: Human-readable Markdown detail. Untrusted: the Hub sanitizes to a no-raw-HTML profile before rendering (spec §9.6). Length is capability-advertised via max_body_bytes, not constrained here.

state.description: Opaque, agent-owned, agent-integrity-sealed resume blob. Hub MUST NOT inspect or log.

client_ref.description: Opaque correlation label. Never a dedup key. Not exposed to resolvers.

idempotency_key.description: Dedup key, scope (agent.id, idempotency_key). REQUIRED for ask/task.

sensitive.description: Message-level sensitivity; excludes value(s) from export/telemetry.

allOf.$comment: >= 0.5 envelopes: agent-form allowed_resolvers entries follow the §4 address grammar (spec §9.1 matching). Pre-0.5 envelopes keep the legacy pattern — hash-bearing principals stay valid for human-inbox traffic (unchanged-wire contract).

`to` and `agent.session` are v0.5 features: an envelope carrying either MUST declare minor >= 5, so the validator never approves a submission whose delivered form (the >= 0.5 inter-agent entry branch of inbound-message.schema.json) could not validate. The same conditional rejects a `#`-bearing agent.id on an addressed/session-bearing submit (spec §4): the Hub would have to attest a `from` the first-#-splits grammar cannot represent — such principals cannot participate in the inter-agent leg (they also cannot register sessions or be addressed).

session.description: Optional registered session of the authenticated principal (v0.5, spec §4.1/§16). Foreign/unknown -> 422; own-but-terminal -> 410. When present, the Caller's mailbox for Response delivery is this session (spec §6). Excluded (with run_id) from the §8.1 idempotency identical-payload comparison.

value.description: The ANSWER payload for this choice — what §6 returns verbatim as `response.value`. MUST be unique within `options` (spec §5.2). Agent-authored, so an agent MAY treat it as known-safe UNLESS `permissions.allow_edit` is true, in which case `response.value` may be human free text (§9.6).

label.description: Human-facing text for this choice. Presentation only; never returned in the Response.

description.description: Optional longer human-facing explanation. Presentation only; never returned in the Response.

options.description: The choices offered for select/confirm. `value` MUST be unique across the array (spec §5.2): §6 returns the chosen `value` and nothing identifying WHICH entry produced it, so a duplicate makes the answer ambiguous. JSON Schema has no uniqueness-by-sub-property keyword, so `uniqueItems` here catches only wholly identical entries — the value-uniqueness rule itself is a Hub obligation (422 at submit), pinned by a §12 class-3 vector, not by this document.

schema.description: REQUIRED for mode=input: a flat JSON Schema describing the ANSWER OBJECT (spec §6 fixes the input answer as an object validating against it). Under mode=input it MUST define at least one entry under `properties`, and any `type` it declares MUST admit an object — a scalar schema admits no valid answer and a property-less one presents nothing to fill in, so both make the ask unanswerable the moment it is accepted (v0.6, spec §5.2). Those constraints are applied by the mode=input conditional below, NOT here: `schema` is meaningless on a select/confirm ask, and a stray one there must not make an otherwise answerable ask invalid. Property types: string/number/boolean/enum. Properties MAY carry `x-ma2h-sensitive: true`.

permissions.description: Which affordances the human is offered (spec §5.2, §7). `allow_accept` was REMOVED in v0.6 — it shipped in v0.1-v0.5 with no semantics in any version, no implementation, and no Response-side anchor. Removal is from the SPEC SURFACE only: a pre-0.6 sender that still carries it is unaffected, because §10 robustness already requires a Hub to ignore unknown fields. A Hub MUST NOT give it meaning.

allow_edit.description: Option-based modes (select/confirm) only: permit the human to answer with a `value` that is NOT a member of `options[].value` — a free-form answer offered alongside the listed options (v0.6, spec §5.2). Default false, which is the pre-v0.6 rule exactly: absent or false, a Hub MUST reject an off-menu value (422). Meaningless for mode=input; a Hub MUST ignore it there. An agent setting this MUST handle an answer outside its own option set and MUST treat it as untrusted human text (§9.6).

allow_respond.description: False removes the answer affordance: the human may only `decline` (spec §5.2, §7).

allow_ignore.description: False removes the decline/ignore affordance (spec §5.2, §7). A human ignoring an ask resolves it `declined` — the v0.1 `ignored` resolution does not exist.

default_on_expire.description: For select: MUST be a member of options[].value (Hub-enforced + conformance vector). For input: an object validating against `schema`, or null.

allowed_resolvers.description: Who may resolve (spec §9.1). On a >= 0.5 envelope an agent-form entry follows the §4 address grammar (the root conditional): principal form matches any session of that principal; a session-qualified form (#sess_...) matches only that exact session — a malformed agent entry could never match an attested actor, leaving the message unresolvable. Pre-0.5 envelopes keep the legacy v0.4 pattern (hash-bearing principals remain valid for human-inbox traffic).

schema.$comment: v0.6: the answer to an input ask is an OBJECT (§6), so `schema` must describe one. `type` may be the string "object" or a WELL-FORMED array containing it — `["object","null"]` is legitimate JSON Schema and answerable, and an earlier draft that tested for the literal string rejected it, breaking a sender that was never broken. The array arm is constrained to the seven JSON Schema type names with uniqueItems: `["object", 42]` and `["object","object"]` are not valid `type` keywords, ajv refuses to compile them, and the ask is then unanswerable exactly as a scalar schema would be. Absent `type` is fine: `properties` is the load-bearing requirement.

allowed_resolvers.description: Who may resolve (spec §9.1). On a >= 0.5 envelope an agent-form entry follows the §4 address grammar (the root conditional): principal form matches any session of that principal; a session-qualified form (#sess_...) matches only that exact session — a malformed agent entry could never match an attested actor, leaving the message unresolvable. Pre-0.5 envelopes keep the legacy v0.4 pattern (hash-bearing principals remain valid for human-inbox traffic).
